course_name_original: Conceção e Fabrico Assistidos por Computador
prerequisites: Knowledge about the Normalization in Mechanical Construction Design (Mechanical Construction Design unit) concepts.
Ability to perform functional analysis of mechanisms (Mechanical Construction Design unit).
Ability to read and elaborate drawings of conception, assembly, and definition of finished product (Mechanical Construction Design unit).
Ability to establish relationships between the conception, definition, and manufacturing phases (Mechanical Construction Design unit).
Knowledge of manufacturing processes and product development (Introduction to Mechanical Engineering unit).
Knowledge of computer programming (Computer Programming unit).

learning_outcomes.text: Know the most common CAD/CAM systems, as well as know how to use the functions offered by them.
Properly execute definition and assembly drawings using CAD systems.
Modeling three-dimensional mechanical system components as well as assembling them using CAD systems.
Automatically obtain assembly and definition drawings of previously three-dimensional modeled mechanical systems or of one of their components using CAD systems.
Perform computational tests/simulations of mechanical resistance using solutions integrated in CAD systems.
Develop computer programs to process information from CAD/CAM/CNC/Simulation systems.
Know the basic principles of numerical control systems and associated machine tools.
Develop numerical control programs for machining operations in lathe and milling machines.

teaching_methods: Lectures (1.5 h T) with analysis of application examples.
Practical laboratory classes (2 h L) with computer exercises for application of concepts.
Extended attending periods for doubt clarification before exams.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (Part II: CNC Programming + CAD/CAM/CNC/Simulation Interface Applications Development)

assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average of the written exam (50%, composed of two 25% parts) and the practical work (50%). An average rating of at least 30% is required for the written exam. Students must attain the required frequency of practical laboratory classes and submit all evaluation components. Two values are subtracted from the final grade for each week of delay in submitting the practical work, up to a maximum of two weeks. For special assessment situations (e.g., TE, DA), students will undergo a written examination covering all course content, a practical assignment, and a possible practical CAD examination.
